lead: TotalEnergies and AMNI took the final investment decision on the $800 million Ima gas project, which President Tinubu hailed as unlocking a 50-year-old resource. Senate President Akpabio and the ADC clashed over whether the President's long absence requires a transfer of power, and the state police amendment was confirmed as the bill sent to state assemblies. The EFCC declared Abdulrasheed Maina wanted, NIMC denied a data breach, and markets weighed the CBN's rate cut.

items.h: $800m Ima gas project reaches final investment decision
items.s: TotalEnergies and AMNI International signed the FID for the offshore development, targeting first gas by the end of 2028. President Tinubu said it unlocks a resource discovered 50 years ago.

items.h: Akpabio and ADC clash over Tinubu's long absence
items.s: The Senate President said there is no need for a transfer of power, while the ADC argued the prolonged absence raises constitutional questions.

items.h: State police bill sent to state assemblies
items.s: The National Assembly said only the amendment creating state police services has so far been transmitted to the 36 assemblies.

items.h: Markets react to CBN's 350bps rate cut
items.s: Businesses welcomed the lower policy rate but said banks must now reduce lending rates.

items.h: EFCC declares Abdulrasheed Maina wanted
items.s: The commission named the former head of the defunct Pension Reform Task Force a wanted person.

items.h: NIMC denies NIN data breach and orders investigation
items.s: The commission rejected claims in a viral video that Nigerians' identity data had been exposed.

items.h: Malami and Fagbemi give conflicting accounts of $200m Mambilla settlement
items.s: The former and current attorneys-general disagreed over the deal with Sunrise Power, and Malami rejected a bribery allegation.

items.h: Makinde denies Oyo got N50bn from Tinubu for airport
items.s: The APM candidate rejected Wike's claim about funding for the Ibadan airport project.

items.h: NMDPRA approves 830,000 tonnes of petrol imports
items.s: Import permits for several marketers were approved ahead of the fourth quarter amid the regulator's legal dispute with Dangote, Premium Times reported.

items.h: Dangote to help 2 million vulnerable women buy refinery shares
items.s: Aliko Dangote announced support for women to take part in the IPO.

items.h: Tinubu calls for African alliance to end raw mineral exports
items.s: The President urged African nations to process critical minerals at home.

items.h: Shettima at UNGA opening; Musa restates peacekeeping commitment
items.s: The Vice President joined world leaders in New York, and the defence minister reaffirmed Nigeria's role in global peacekeeping.

items.h: Oyedele calls for cheaper capital for African infrastructure
items.s: The finance minister urged the international community to expand affordable financing.

items.h: INEC seeks adequate funding for 2027 security and logistics
items.s: Chairman Joash Amupitan said proper funding is critical.

items.h: Tinubu and Uzodimma urge police impartiality
items.s: At CARSPO in Owerri, the IGP told politicians to compete with ideas.

items.h: 5,000 PDP members join APC in Ogun
items.s: Defectors were received at a rally in Ilaro.

items.h: Masari says Tinubu has the best plans he has seen
items.s: The former Katsina governor praised the President's programme.

items.h: Umahi plans 4,000 influencers to showcase projects
items.s: The works minister said influencers will publicise infrastructure delivered under Tinubu.

items.h: First 105km of coastal highway to be paved by November
items.s: Works Minister David Umahi gave the timeline for the Lagos-Calabar road.

items.h: Kano drug taskforce arrests 380, secures 230 convictions
items.s: The multi-agency team also seized illicit substances.

items.h: NSCDC arrests three over NNPC pipeline vandalism in Kwali
items.s: A truck carrying 17 vandalised pipes was seized in Dafa.

items.h: Group mourns 37 mining suspects as panel begins work
items.s: CREAP Africa Initiative expressed grief over the deaths in Niger State.

items.h: Firms to capture flared gas for power
items.s: AfricaGTC and Energy Ventures will convert 5 MMscfd of flared gas.

items.h: First self-service fuel station opens in Abuja
items.s: Sunbeth Energies opened the station in Wuse.

items.h: Airtel Money plans London IPO
items.s: The mobile money business announced plans to list on the LSE.

items.h: Kenya to launch Dangote-backed $17bn refinery on 30 September
items.s: President William Ruto is expected at the Lamu groundbreaking.

items.h: Financial inclusion rises to 79%
items.s: EFInA said 94.2 million adults use at least one financial service.

items.h: ECOWAS warns climate change could displace 32 million
items.s: The bloc said displacement threatens regional stability by 2050.

items.h: Edible oil tanker drivers suspend strike
items.s: The FG and DSS intervened a day before it was due to start.

items.h: Talks begin on moving dry port functions to NPERA
items.s: The ports regulator and NPA discussed the transfer.

items.h: World Bank-backed erosion work starts in Birnin Kebbi
items.s: Gully control began in Badariya and Dukku Malala.

items.h: TRCN plans AI training for teachers in all 774 LGAs
items.s: The council is working with GMind.

items.h: Troost-Ekong converts to Islam
items.s: The former Super Eagles captain recited the Shahadah in Doha.

items.h: Super Eagles begin qualifiers with 21 players in camp
items.s: Madagascar's Rayan Raveloson said his team has no fear before Friday's game in Uyo.
